title: Security, privacy, and resource abuse
note: Written before the Stage 7 sandbox harness ran. Every assigned scenario is expected to PASS. Any observed FAIL, BLOCKED or NOT RUN is a provisional agent result requiring parent review; this file is not self-approval and makes no release claim. All fixed hashes below come from the frozen approved tarball, the parent-accepted Stage 2 R1/S3 fixtures, or pre-run fixture files; none is copied from a Stage 7 observation.

expectedTarball.rule: The approved actual tarball is hash-verified before upload and installed as bytes in an empty consumer. A different hash stops the stage; no repository alias, workspace or symlink is accepted.

golden.source: Parent-accepted Stage 2 R1 S2-08 fix/record; not a Stage 7 observation.

limits.note: These are declared test caps, not product performance promises. Extreme-input measurements are bounded samples and make no constant-time or unbounded-input claim. Fatal V8 OOM is an engine/runtime resource limit, not a package contract requirement.

trustBoundary.statement: The validated high-level renderers (ditherFace and the eight direct renderers) must treat seed and name as opaque strings and must never emit executable markup, handler attributes, javascript/data-html URIs or external references. Low-level rect, disc and asciiGrid accept trusted colors, ids and SVG fragments and are documented as non-sanitizers; escaping behavior is text-content-only. S7-01 records the low-level boundary as expected behaviour, not as a vulnerability.

S7-01.title: SVG injection
S7-01.expected: Every high-level seed, name and option injection payload across all eight styles plus all eight direct renderers produces non-empty standalone SVG that parses as well-formed XML, contains no script/foreignObject/iframe/object/embed/image element, no on* handler, no javascript: or data:text/html URI, no external href/src/url, no unresolved local id reference and no XML-invalid character. A real XML parser and a real browser both parse/import every unique output; the browser executes no payload, opens no alert and attempts no external request. Options payloads throw documented errors. Trusted low-level rect/disc/asciiGrid concatenation is recorded as documented trust, not misclassified as a high-level sanitizer failure.

S7-02.title: UI injection
S7-02.expected: Payloads in seed, name, status/source/code regions and URL parameters are rendered as inert text or textarea values. No new script/img/iframe element or event-handler attribute appears in the preview, gallery, usage code, status or manual-copy panel; no payload executes or alerts. Prototype-like parameters (__proto__, constructor, prototype) and malformed/duplicate/long parameters cause no prototype pollution and no unexpected window global mutation; documented fallbacks/precedence apply.

S7-03.title: CSP compatibility
S7-03.expected: site/_headers and the local server both send the same strict CSP with no unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval or wildcard source, plus no-referrer/nosniff/DENY headers. The normal Chromium site UI and all eight bundled renderers match the frozen installed-package golden under that CSP with zero unexpected CSP violations, console errors or page errors; a data:image/svg+xml image loads under img-src data: with no violation. Deliberate inline script, cross-origin script and inline handler payloads are blocked and their expected violations are recorded separately; the cross-origin attempt never reaches the controlled sink. The site bundle contains no eval/new Function and no local/source-alias path. WebKit is additionally probed for the Stage 6 stylesheet warning: securitypolicyviolation fields (blockedURI, sourceFile, line, effectiveDirective), stylesheet origins/style nodes/style-attribute mutations, all-eight-renderer parity, data URL image, select functionality, and the Stage 6 manual-copy fallback are captured. A control matrix (blank page, generated SVG insertion, plain/presentation SVG, app without JS, reduced HTML, select-only, inputs-only, details-only, CSS-only) must distinguish app inline SVG presentation styles, native app form controls, and browser/tool-injected stylesheets. If the warning is not reproduced, the precise no-attribution limit is recorded rather than ignored. Expected: the Stage 6 warning is the native select style-src-attr report under WebKit; it does not block code, SVG fill or select functionality, and screenshot-only web-inspector bootstrap style injection is a separate tool artifact.

S7-04.title: Referrer and privacy
S7-04.expected: Under the served Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, a real outgoing link to a controlled loopback sink sends no Referer header and no seed URL; the sink page document.referrer is empty and no third-party request is made. The privacy copy accurately says inputs stay in the page URL for sharing and may appear in browser history, tells users not to use a secret or email, the seed is visibly present in the address-bar URL, URL edits use replaceState (no per-keystroke history entries), and the visible Copy link action copies the visible current URL rather than a hidden secret. External production links are not clicked.

S7-05.title: Network behavior
S7-05.expected: After page assets load, all eight styles render with the browser network disabled, all eight outputs match the frozen golden, and zero requests/failures are attempted during offline rendering. A Node probe that guards http/https/net/dns/fetch/WebSocket renders all eight installed-package styles with zero network calls and matching hashes. No external or dynamic font is used: no @font-face or third-party font URL, no font request, and ASCII styles use only a system monospace stack.

S7-06.title: Secrets and excluded data
S7-06.expected: A pinned conservative classifier scans tracked source, the actual tarball and its exact allowlist, qualification fixtures, and this stage's raw logs. It finds no credential-shaped token, private-key block, auth-like assignment or excluded backup/env/auth file; findings, if any, would be reported as redacted file+line+type only and require human review. The tracked Stage 3 pnpm .npmrc fixture is declared as a reviewed false positive (no auth token) and is reported, not hidden. No scan reads home auth material or prints a potential secret. Built site and installed package contain no local host path, runtime env reference, sensitive environment value or excluded file. A clearly fake synthetic canary is detected by the same classifier without writing the canary value to evidence.

S7-07.title: Extreme inputs
S7-07.expected: With a declared 10s/256 MB child cap, each of the eight styles renders a 1 MB seed, pathological Unicode (combining marks, bidi/zero-width controls, NUL/C0 and a lone surrogate), and large finite px (1e9 and Number.MAX_VALUE) without timeout or crash; all valid outputs parse as well-formed SVG/XML. NaN, Infinity, zero, negative, string/null px, numeric name, unknown/injection style, null/array options and numeric seed are rejected with documented TypeError/RangeError/Error classes for all eight styles. CPU/wall time and memory are recorded; no constant-time or unbounded-input promise is made. A documented 32-bit FNV-1a collision, if found, renders identical bytes and is not classified as a vulnerability.

S7-08.title: Resource limits
S7-08.expected: Declared caps are 256 MB child heap and 10s per child, with an 8s internal deadline for a huge batch. The huge batch pauses at its bounded deadline without exceeding the target or host memory; the sandbox and a fresh render remain responsive. A disposable 32 MB-heap child that retains renders terminates with a V8 heap/OOM condition before the 10s wall cap, is fully reaped, and does not claim success. The report distinguishes engine/runtime OOM from package contract behaviour and makes no claim that the library must catch fatal OOM or provide invented safety under unlimited input.

expected: actual SVG checker detects script element, inline handler and external/javascript URI and passes a clean generated SVG
actual CSP checker detects a missing header and unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval and passes the shipped strict header
actual secret classifier detects a clearly fake synthetic canary and passes clean text without logging the canary
network interceptor blocks and records a synthetic outbound attempt without a real connection
normal clean inputs pass every positive checker

environment.browser: Chromium (primary) and WebKit (Stage 6 CSP diagnostic) via pinned @playwright/test 1.64.1
